findings.title: A broken effort can never be opened in the pane, so CT-2's broken-history path is unreachable there
quotes: each effort row is a `Button` with `key` = the slug
return False, commit(), f"{slug} · broken: {e.file}, {e.where}"
if (p[1]?.startsWith('broken:')) return [{ slug, error: p.slice(1).join(' · ') }]
Given an effort whose `history.jsonl` has an unreadable line, when the drill-down is shown, then the timeline names the error and the other sections still render.
findings.fix: make CT-12 put a Button on error rows that have a slug too, opening the same drill-down. Add a pane test that presses a `broken:` row and sees the timeline error alongside the other sections. Otherwise, narrow AC-4 to the CLI with the human's agreement.

sources.situation: `history.jsonl` gets a whole non-JSON line (TC-5's case). `flow.read` raises `Broken`, `status_row` prints `slug · broken: history.jsonl, line 2`, and the pane makes it an error row, drawn as red `Text` rather than an effort row. CT-12 puts Buttons only on effort rows, so the human can't select the effort and AC-4's drill-down never appears. TC-5 only tests the CLI.

findings.reason: register.tsx renders `error` rows as plain `<Text color="error">` (lines 237-241) and parseStatus turns `broken:` rows into error lines (line 41). CT-12 puts a Button only on effort rows, so AC-4's pane path is unreachable, and TC-5 only tests the CLI.
findings.note: Broken effort rows are Buttons opening the drill-down; TC-37 tests it (CT-12, CT-14)

findings.reason: skills/install/SKILL.md says "the human's answer to one question" and its Outputs lists no mods. CT-15 changes only the steps and "When to stop", so the Inputs and Outputs lines would be stale. The repo rule in CLAUDE.md requires them to be stated.

findings.title: CT-10's install command is not the one the mods' own README documents
quotes: `<claude> plugin install <mod> --marketplace <mods_dir()> --scope local --json`
claude plugin marketplace add ~/nio/tools/claude-mods
claude plugin install background-nio-commands@nio-mods
findings.fix: either cite in CT-10 the research finding that shows `--marketplace` exists, or use the documented `marketplace add <mods_dir()>` then `plugin install <mod>@nio-mods --scope local`. In either case, say what `@nio:install` does when the registered marketplace path is gone (reinstall rather than report "already installed").

sources.situation: the existing README installs in two steps: add the marketplace, then install `<mod>@nio-mods`. CT-10 relies on a `--marketplace <path>` flag that none of the files I was given show. In a target project, `mods_dir()` is a path inside the installed package, which can move when `uv tool install` reinstalls nio, for example under a new Python version. That would leave the registered marketplace pointing at a folder that no longer exists. Only the NIO_E2E tests (TC-20 to TC-22) would catch a wrong flag, and they don't run by default.

findings.note: CT-10 cites RF-2 (claude plugin install --help documents --marketplace <path>) and says a listed mod is left as is

findings.title: TC-34 passes on today's code
quotes: Assert: the recorded list is unchanged (no file added, removed or modified).
findings.fix: assert exit 0 and that `cost` and `memory` are not `{"error": ...}` before comparing the file list, and move TC-34 to the last story that delivers CT-6 or CT-7 (or list it under both US-4 and US-5).

sources.situation: today `nio flow show` is an argparse error (the `flow` subparsers have no `show`, exit 2), so it writes no file and TC-34 is green before any work. In Foundation, CT-6 and CT-7, whose index and usage reads are what could write, aren't built yet. So a `show` that crashes early, or that never builds memory or cost, passes too. The test can't fail at red and doesn't prove NFR-2 for the code that matters.

findings.reason: TC-34 only asserts that the file list is unchanged and does not check exit code or section content. It sits in Foundation, where CT-6 and CT-7 aren't built yet, so it passes when `show` is absent or crashes early.
findings.note: TC-34 asserts exit 0 and no error in cost or memory before comparing files; now in US-4

findings.title: TC-25 passes when every section is an error
quotes: Assert: exit 0; `json.loads(stdout)` has the keys `timeline`, `juries`, `tasks`, `cost`, `memory` (plus `slug`, `stage`)
or `{"error": "<text>"}` when building that section raised (FR-13): one section's failure never stops the others
findings.fix: also assert no section is a dict with an `error` key (the setup provides data for all five).

sources.situation: CT-2 turns any exception in a section into `{"error": ...}`, so a `show` whose five section builders all raise (e.g. not yet written in Foundation, or a NameError) still prints the five keys and exit 0. The setup has history, a ledger, tasks and events, but nothing checks that they reached the output.

findings.note: TC-25 asserts no section is an error dict

findings.title: TC-11's per-line `state` makes the final state.json ambiguous
quotes: `claim` for the second, with `state: {"claims": {"task": <it>}, "attempts": {<it>: 2}}`; for the first task of E-2 `claim` then a `review` with `passed` false, with `state: {"attempts": {<it>: 1}}`
Observable: each task row's status and attempt count equal the values in `state.json`.
findings.fix: give the one final state.json explicitly, e.g. `{"claims": {"task": <second>}, "attempts": {<second>: 2, <E-2 first>: 1}}`, with attempts values that differ from what history alone would give.

sources.situation: state.json holds the state the last history write leaves. If each `state:` given here is the whole state for that write, the final state has `attempts` only for E-2's task and no claim. Then the expected "`status \"claimed\"`, `attempts 2`" for the second task can't hold, and the writer must guess whether to merge. One reading fails a correct build. The other lets a builder that reads attempts from history (as `usage.attempts` does) pass.

findings.note: TC-11 sets one final state.json explicitly with attempts history can't give
